data.title: Clotrimazole (cream, solution, dusting powder, paint, soap)
data.body:
_Topicals · I Antifungals — Azoles_

**Class:** Imidazole antifungal

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits fungal 14-α-demethylase → ergosterol depletion; fungistatic (fungicidal at high concentration)
- Broad spectrum: dermatophytes, Candida, Malassezia; some Gram-positive bacteria

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Cutaneous candidiasis (intertrigo, napkin candidiasis, paronychia), tinea corporis/cruris/pedis, pityriasis versicolor
- Dusting powder: prevention in moist areas (groin, toe webs, folds) after the cream clears infection
- Mouth paint 1%: oral thrush; vaginal tablets/cream: vulvovaginal candidiasis
- Solution: hairy areas, nails folds, ear (otomycosis)
- Soap: adjunct only (short contact time)

## Dose & formulations
- Cream 1%: twice daily, continue 2 weeks after clinical cure (usually 2–4 weeks)
- Powder 1%: once or twice daily on dry skin
- Mouth paint 1%: 3–4 times daily for 1–2 weeks

## Adverse effects
- Burning, irritation, rare contact dermatitis

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe — preferred topical azole for vaginal candidiasis in pregnancy.

## Viva points
- Workhorse imidazole for candidiasis
- Powders are for prevention, not treatment of active infection
- Clotrimazole + steroid combinations are widely misused (see the combination post)

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.42; Khopkar ch.19. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
